The Office of the Provost publishes the undergraduate grade-appeal procedure. Grade appeals require supporting documentation; possible grounds include computational error, factual information not in evidence when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on needing a higher grade, or on a grade penalty for an Academic Integrity Policy violation, are not considered. After the student and instructor cannot agree, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean does not support the appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within twenty calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination. Include your position and evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. The Provost’s Office may reject a petition without clear evidence of a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. The Provost or designee’s decision is final. [1][2]

The Public Health Minor is five courses (20 credits). [1] You must take BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY and PHLT 290 TOPICS. Choose one from each of these groups: statistics or research methods; health policy and management; social and behavioral science; and global or population health. [1]

The catalog lists these options in those groups: [1]
• Statistics/research methods: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS.
• Health policy/management: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY.
• Social/behavioral science: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; PHLT 390 TOPICS.
• Global/population health: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS.

For either procedure, grade appeals require supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based on wanting a higher grade or an Academic Integrity penalty are not considered. After a degree is conferred, that degree’s academic record cannot be adjusted. [2]

Undergraduate: If you and the instructor cannot agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean’s written decision does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days of that decision. Include your position and evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. The Provost will reject requests without clear evidence of a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview; the decision is final. [1]

Graduate: Bring your written appeal, by email or certified letter with supporting documentation, to the faculty member no later than 20 calendar days after grades are posted. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. For undergraduate grade appeals, the College considers appeals only with documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not available when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based on simply needing a higher grade, or a grade penalty for an Academic Integrity violation, are not considered. A degree’s academic record cannot be adjusted after the degree is conferred. [2]

If you and the instructor cannot agree and you want to pursue an appeal, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference with the instructor. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost by written statement (email or certified letter) within twenty calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination. Include evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. The Provost may reject petitions without clear evidence of factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview; this stage follows full deliberative discussion at instructor and Dean levels. The decision is final and is due within 15 calendar days. [1]

For graduate appeals, the page excerpt says that after an unfavorable Program Director opinion, you may submit a written petition to the Dean who supervises the program, with evidence contradicting the decision or information previously unavailable. The Dean considers appeals that have received full deliberative discussion at faculty and Program Director levels, decides within 15 calendar days, and the decision is final. The excerpt does not give the initial graduate appeal deadline. [15]

Financial Aid says part-time means fewer than 12 credits; federal aid requires at least 6 credits. If you go from 12 credits to 6, your federal Pell Grant will be reduced, but you can keep federal loans. State aid may be canceled, and institutional grants or scholarships may be reduced or taken away. [1, 6]

Timing matters: before the 100% and 50% refund points, aid is adjusted if you drop below full-time. After the 100% or 50% refund period, federal aid “should not be affected” if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when it is fully disbursed. [1, 2]

Academic Scholarships and Ramapo grants may be reduced or taken away below 12 credits; an Out-of-State Housing grant is canceled if you can no longer live on campus. Contact the Office of Financial Aid before making a change that takes you below full-time, and meet with it to discuss how dropping a class may affect your aid. [2, 3]

You must also meet SAP standards: at annual review, undergraduates need a cumulative Ramapo GPA of at least 2.0 and graduate students at least 3.0; students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits toward graduation requirements. [4]
